Ringed space

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Geometry and topology Algebraic geometry
OurBigBook.com Words: 17k Articles: 349
A ringed space (X,OX​) is a topological space X equipped with a sheaf of rings OX​. A morphism consists of a continuous map f:X→Y and a compatible morphism f−1OY​→OX​.

Morphism of ringed spaces

Words: 26
Ringed space OurBigBook.com
A morphism of ringed spaces f:(X,OX​)→(Y,OY​) consists of a continuous map f:X→Y and a morphism of sheaves of rings f−1OY​→OX​.

Sheaf of rings

Words: 97 Articles: 1
Ringed space OurBigBook.com
A sheaf of rings assigns a ring O(U) to every open set, restriction homomorphisms to inclusions, and satisfies local identity and gluing. It supplies the local functions on a ringed space.
This is a ring-valued Sheaf (mathematics), with ring homomorphisms as restriction maps.

Sheaf of topological rings

Words: 55
Sheaf of rings OurBigBook.com
A sheaf of topological rings takes values in topological rings, with continuous restriction maps. For an open cover, the sheaf condition is an equalizer of the product of sections on the cover and the product on pairwise overlaps, in the category of topological rings. The structure sheaf of a formal scheme is an inverse limit of discrete structure sheaves with this topology.
// Target: algebra.bigb

Sheaf of modules

Words: 9k Articles: 167
Ringed space OurBigBook.com
For a ringed space (X,OX​), a sheaf of OX​-modules is a sheaf F such that every F(U) is an OX​(U)-module and restriction maps preserve scalar multiplication.
The underlying object is a Sheaf (mathematics) with compatible local module actions.

Internal Hom sheaf (HomOX​​(F,G))

Words: 54
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For sheaves of modules F,G on a ringed space, the internal Hom sheaf assigns to an open U the module of sheaf morphisms F∣U​→G∣U​ respecting OU​. Compatible morphisms glue, so this is a sheaf. Its global sections are precisely the global module-sheaf morphisms. For a locally free sheaf F of finite rank it is F∨⊗G.

Local system

Words: 26
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
A local system is a locally constant sheaf of modules, for example the integral cohomology of fibres of a smooth proper family of compact complex manifolds. Parallel continuation around loops gives its monodromy representation.

Rational section of a sheaf of modules (Rat(F)=lim​U dense open​Γ(U,F))

Words: 347 Articles: 4
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
A rational section is a section on a dense open subset, with two representatives identified when they agree on a common dense open subset. Intersecting representatives' domains defines addition. Multiplication by a similarly represented rational function on an algebraic variety makes these classes a module over the ring Rat(X). For an irreducible variety, this ring is its function field.

Rational principal part (Rat(F)/FP​)

Words: 242 Articles: 2
Rational section of a sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For a locally free sheaf on an irreducible variety, the stalk inclusion identifies sections regular near P inside its rational sections. The quotient records the obstruction to regularity at that point. This definition does not assume a nonsingular point or a discrete valuation parameter.
Rational principal-parts resolution on an algebraic curve (0→F→R(F)→P(F)→0)
Words: 203 Articles: 1
Rational principal part OurBigBook.com
On an irreducible algebraic curve, let R(F) be the constant rational-section sheaf and put P(F)(U)=⨁P∈U​Rat(F)/FP​. Every open subset is quasi-compact, so compatible finite-support families glue with finite support. Its stalk at P is the displayed rational-principal-part quotient. A rational section is regular outside finitely many points, making its principal-part map well defined. The resulting sequence is stalkwise exact. Both right-hand sheaves are flasque, and consequently H1(X,F) is the cokernel of the global principal-part map and Hq(X,F)=0 for q≥2. The curve and Zariski-topology hypotheses distinguish finite support here from locally finite pole sets in complex analysis.
Affine principal-parts interpolation for a locally free sheaf
Words: 99
Rational principal-parts resolution on an algebraic curve OurBigBook.com
Let X be an irreducible affine curve, A=k[X], K=FracA, and F=M be locally free. Given finitely many classes in MK​/MmP​​, choose one nonzero a∈A clearing denominators of representatives. The ring A/(a) is Artinian and is the product of its finitely many local factors. Hence M/aM≅⨁P∈V(a)​(M/aM)mP​​. Prescribe avP​ modulo aMmP​​ at the requested points and zero at the other zeros of a. Lift this tuple to w∈M; the section w/a has exactly the requested rational principal parts and no others. This proves surjectivity without assuming the curve is nonsingular.

Stalk inclusion into rational sections of a locally free sheaf (FP​↪Rat(F))

Words: 55
Rational section of a sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
On an irreducible variety, every nonempty open subset is dense, so a germ determines a rational section. For a locally free sheaf, this map is injective: a local section which vanishes on a dense open has all its regular coefficient functions zero, hence is zero. Local freeness is important; a section of a torsion sheaf can vanish generically without having zero germ.

Coherent analytic sheaf (F a coherent OX​-module)

Words: 49
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
On a complex manifold, a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of holomorphic functions is coherent analytic if it is locally finitely generated and the kernel of every morphism Or→F is locally finitely generated. The structure sheaf and locally free finite-rank sheaves are examples. Cartan theorem B gives vanishing of their higher sheaf cohomology on a Stein manifold.

Dual of a sheaf (F∨=HomOX​​(F,OX​))

Words: 57
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
The dual is the sheaf of modules whose sections on U are module-sheaf morphisms F∣U​→OU​. For a locally free sheaf of finite rank, the dual is locally free of the same rank and the natural double-dual map is an isomorphism. General coherent sheaves need not have this property: a skyscraper at a point of positive-dimensional projective space has zero ordinary sheaf dual.

Injective sheaf of modules

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
On a ringed space (X,OX​), an injective module sheaf is an injective object in the category of sheaves of modules over OX​. Its defining extension property concerns module-sheaf morphisms; it is distinct from injectivity solely in the category of sheaves of abelian groups.

Injective module sheaves are flasque

Words: 56
Injective sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
For opens U⊆V⊆X, there is a monomorphism between the extensions by zero of OU​ and OV​. Morphisms from these sheaves into an injective sheaf of modules I identify with sections on U and V, respectively. The injective object extension property therefore makes the restriction I(V)→I(U) surjective, proving that I is flasque. The argument applies to any ringed space.

Stalk of a sheaf (Fx​)

Words: 347 Articles: 7
Sheaf of modules OurBigBook.com
The stalk Fx​ is the direct limit of F(U) over neighborhoods U of x. A morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism or forms an exact sequence exactly when it does so on every stalk.

Costalk (ix!​E)

Words: 35
Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
The derived costalk at x is ix!​E, where ix​:{x}↪X. It computes local cohomology supported at x. On an oriented N-manifold the constant sheaf has costalk Q[−N], whose cohomology is in degree N.

Stalk functor for presheaves of sets (F↦Fx​)

Words: 93 Articles: 1
Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
For presheaves of sets, Fx​=lim​U∋x​F(U). This functor preserves finite limits because the neighborhood system is filtered and filtered colimits commute with finite limits in sets. Its right adjoint sends a set S to the presheaf taking the value S on opens containing x and the singleton on other opens.
Joint stalk functor on sheaves of sets (F↦(Fx​)x∈X​)
Words: 49
Stalk functor for presheaves of sets OurBigBook.com
The joint stalk functor Sh(X)→SetX is faithful: equality of germs makes two images of a section locally equal, and the sheaf uniqueness axiom makes them globally equal. Its right adjoint is the product of the set-valued skyscraper sheaves at all points. The Beck comonadicity theorem then makes the joint stalk functor comonadic.

Skyscraper sheaf

Words: 123 Articles: 1
Stalk of a sheaf OurBigBook.com
For a point inclusion i:{x}↪X and an abelian group A, the skyscraper sheaf i∗​A has sections A on opens containing x and zero on other opens. Its restriction maps are identities or maps to zero. If A=0, its nonzero stalks occur at every point of the closure {x}​: exactly those points whose every neighbourhood contains x. Thus the familiar assertion that only the stalk at x is nonzero requires x to be a closed point. It is always flasque, giving the stated skyscraper sheaf cohomology.
Skyscraper sheaf cohomology (H0(X,i∗​A)=A,Hi>0(X,i∗​A)=0)
Words: 39
Skyscraper sheaf OurBigBook.com
For any point inclusion i:{x}↪X, the skyscraper sheaf i∗​A has restriction maps that are identities or maps to zero. It is flasque, so its higher sheaf cohomology vanishes and its global sections are A. This requires no assumption that x is closed.

A closed point on the affine chart is cut out by an irreducible polynomial f(t), whose divisor is that point minus deg(f) times infinity. Thus a line bundle of degree d is O(d).

Affine plane OurBigBook.com
The points of the real affine plane as a scheme are its prime ideals: the zero ideal, the principal ideals of irreducible real polynomials, and its maximal ideals. The latter have residue field R or C, by the Zariski lemma and the real closed field property. They correspond respectively to real coordinate pairs and conjugate pairs of nonreal complex coordinate pairs. Thus the scheme contains both nonclosed generic points and closed points absent from the real locus. Its topology is the Zariski topology, and its structure sheaf has sections R[x,y]h​ on each principal open subscheme D(h).

An algebraic variety that is separated over its ground field. Two affine open charts have an affine intersection: their intersection is the inverse image of the closed diagonal inside the product of the two affine charts. This ensures a finite affine cover is acyclic for quasi-coherent sheaves.

For a finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes, separatedness is equivalent to uniqueness in every lifting problem SpecK→X over SpecR→Y, where R is a valuation ring with fraction field K.

A morphism is proper when it is separated, of finite type, and universally closed. Properness is stable under base change and composition.
Complete variety
Words: 65
Proper morphism OurBigBook.com
A variety over a field k is complete when its map to Speck is universally closed: after any base change, projection sends closed subsets to closed subsets. For a separated finite-type variety, this is equivalent to being proper. In the classical algebraically closed setting one may test projections X×Y→Y for arbitrary varieties. Images of rational points over a non-algebraically-closed field must not replace geometric images.
Proper affine morphisms are finite (SpecB→SpecA proper⟹B finite over A)
Words: 131
Proper morphism OurBigBook.com
For a finite-type affine morphism of Noetherian schemes, apply its valuative lifting property to each domain quotient B/q for a minimal prime and all valuation rings of its fraction field containing the image of A. The lift forces B/q into every such valuation ring, hence makes it integral over that image. For each b∈B, multiply the finitely many resulting monic equations. Its value at b lies in the nilradical. The nilradical of a Noetherian ring is nilpotent, so a power of this monic polynomial annihilates b. Thus B is integral over A. Finitely many algebra generators, each satisfying a monic equation, have their powers reduced to finitely many monomials, proving that B is a finite A-module. Nilpotents cannot be ignored in this proof.

Proper morphism OurBigBook.com
Suppose gf is proper, f is surjective, and g is separated and of finite type. Surjectivity of scheme morphisms is preserved by base change: a nonempty fiber remains nonempty after a residue-field extension. After any base change to Z, for a closed subset C of the new target of f, its inverse image is closed and has image g(C) under the proper composite. Thus g(C) is closed. This proves universal closedness of g, completing the three conditions for properness.

In a proper flat family of algebraic curves, if the first sheaf cohomology of a line bundle vanishes on every fibre of an open set, its direct image there is a vector bundle of rank given by the Riemann-Roch theorem and commutes with arbitrary base change. Locally a finite free complex computes both fibre sheaf cohomology groups. Vanishing of the last cokernel makes its last map surjective; splitting that map leaves a finite locally free kernel in degree zero. This is the mechanism behind charts of the Picard scheme of a curve and evaluation descriptions of the theta divisor.

For a line bundle M on C×T, with C a smooth projective curve, this function is locally constant. Twist both M and M−1 by a large power of an ample line bundle on C. Near a chosen fiber their first sheaf cohomology groups vanish. The Riemann-Roch theorem and upper semicontinuity of their zeroth sheaf cohomology groups then bound the degree from above and below by the degree on that fiber. A morphism i:Z→X is a closed immersion when it identifies Z homeomorphically with a closed subset of X and the morphism OX​→i∗​OZ​ is surjective. Affine-locally it has the form Spec(A/I)→SpecA.

Words: 85
Closed immersion OurBigBook.com
A nonempty flat closed immersion of finite presentation into a connected scheme is an isomorphism. On a chart it is A→A/I with I finitely generated. At a prime containing I, the quotient is a finite flat module over the local ring, hence free of rank one, so I vanishes there. Finite generation extends this vanishing to a neighbourhood. Thus the image is open as well as closed; connectedness makes it all of the target, and the ideal is everywhere zero. Without finite presentation the conclusion can fail.

Closed immersion OurBigBook.com
A surjective ring homomorphism A→B=A/I identifies the spectrum of a ring B with the closed subset V(I) and induces a surjective map of structure sheaves. Conversely, the direct image sheaf of OSpecB​ under an affine morphism is the sheaf associated with the A-module B: its sections on D(a) are Bϕ(a)​. The cokernel of the structure-sheaf map is therefore associated with the module cokernel of A→B. If the sheaf map is surjective, all localizations of that cokernel vanish and the module cokernel is zero. This proves the converse without assuming global sections preserve arbitrary sheaf surjections.

Words: 211 Articles: 3
Closed subscheme OurBigBook.com
A projective complete intersection is a closed subscheme of a projective space defined by a homogeneous regular sequence of positive degrees. A length-r sequence in k[t0​,…,tN​] gives dimension N−r when r≤N. Sheafifying its successive quotient sequences gives exact restriction sequences of twisting sheaves on projective space, allowing computation of its sheaf cohomology. It need not be smooth or reduced.

Words: 47
Projective complete intersection OurBigBook.com
A projective complete intersection defined by a regular sequence in a polynomial ring has pure codimension equal to the sequence length and has no embedded associated primes. Thus its components account for the whole degree, with their generic multiplicities. This fact excludes hidden embedded points when a contained curve already has the full intersection degree.

Words: 73
Projective complete intersection OurBigBook.com
For a length-r homogeneous regular sequence of positive degrees in PkN​, with r<N, the global regular functions on its projective complete intersection are exactly k. In the successive restriction sequences, intermediate cohomology vanishing for a projective complete intersection makes the first-cohomology group on the preceding stage zero. Inductively all negative twists have zero global sections, so at twist zero the restriction of constants is an isomorphism. The positive-dimension assumption is essential: a zero-dimensional complete intersection can have more global functions, including nilpotents.

Both adjacent groups in the long exact sequence in sheaf cohomology vanish precisely in the indicated range.

A finite locally free sheaf of ideals on a reduced scheme has rank at most one at every point. The affine plane with doubled origin is formed by gluing two copies of Ak2​ by the identity away from the origin. The overlap is the punctured affine plane, so this scheme is nonseparated and the two-open affine cover is not acyclic for the structure sheaf.

A scheme is semi-separated when the intersection of any two affine open subsets is affine, equivalently when its diagonal is affine. This condition makes affine covers acyclic for quasi-coherent sheaves.

Ringed space OurBigBook.com
For a continuous map f:X→Y, the direct-image functor sends a sheaf F on X to the sheaf V↦F(f−1V) on Y, and sends sheaf morphisms to their induced maps on sections. Its output is a direct image sheaf.

Ringed space OurBigBook.com
For a continuous map f:X→Y, the inverse-image functor takes a sheaf on Y to the sheafification of its local inverse-image presheaf on X. It is left adjoint to the direct image functor. For sheaves of modules on ringed spaces, extension of scalars gives the separate pullback of a sheaf of modules.

Valuative criterion

Words: 51
Ringed space OurBigBook.com
Valuative criteria test properties of scheme morphisms by extending a lift from the generic point of the spectrum of a valuation ring to the whole spectrum. Under the usual finiteness hypotheses, uniqueness characterizes separatedness, existence characterizes universal closedness, and existence with uniqueness characterizes properness. The valuative criterion for separatedness and valuative criterion for properness are the respective specific statements.
